title: OpalWave - model portability, multilingual and tool-calling discovery
next_steps: Share model latency/cost matrix and bench scripts
action_items: Maya: send pricing tier sheet and benchmark scripts by 2027-07-09
Diego: propose pilot architecture diagram and suggest quantization/profile options by 2027-07-12
Priya: provide representative prompt set and traffic profile by 2027-07-10
summary: Initial technical discovery for OpalWave evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for a multilingual content-moderation and personalization pipeline. Main concerns: context length for multi-turn personalization, cost/latency tradeoffs, tool-calling (external knowledge connectors), and security/keys. Agreement to run a pilot; Redwood to provide benchmarks and security docs.
topics: model selection (open models), context window needs, multilingual quality, tool calling/webhook patterns, hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS, rollout strategy
transcript:
00:00 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. we know it's a busy week so appreciate the time. i'm maya from Redwood, i'm the account lead for OpalWave. quick roundtable?
00:08 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): hey maya, liam here, cto at opalwave. we run recommendations and personalization for streaming clients.
00:15 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): priya, ml engineer, primarily on the inference side.
00:19 - Speaker 4 (Jamal Reed): jamal, product, i'll be driving success metrics.
00:22 - Speaker 5 (Elena Kovacs): elena from security — quick heads up, i'll ask about compliance and key mgmt.
00:27 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): amazing. diego and sofia from our solutions team are on — diego will lead the technical parts.
00:34 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): hi everyone, thanks. quick agenda: understand their current stack and constraints, clarify workloads and SLOs, discuss model/capacity options, and outline a pilot. sound good?
00:42 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): yep. our core ask — we want a unified inference path that can do moderation, personalization (multi-turn), and some tool calls (search for up-to-date metadata). we want to weigh open-models for cost vs managed offerings.
00:58 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): great — can you share current traffic and latency targets?
01:03 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): typical peak qps per region is around 120 rps for personalization endpoint, p50 latency target is < 200ms token timestep? um, well, for the UI we need generation latency end-to-end under ~600ms usually. some batch async jobs can tolerate 2s.
01:24 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): ok that's helpful. and context lengths — how many tokens of history?
01:29 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): personalization needs 6-12k tokens for full session history plus metadata. moderation short contexts — 1-2k. multilingual support: EN/ES/FR/DE and occasional JP/KR.
01:43 - Speaker 5 (Elena Kovacs): security — we need SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. also, any egress to 3rd-party APIs for tool-calls needs to be controllable.
01:55 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): absolutely. we've supported those controls in private and dedicated networks, and hosted with customer-managed keys for enterprise. diego, can you talk model options?
02:05 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): sure — for the workload described, we usually split responsibilities: smaller, faster LMs for moderation and deterministic reranking, and larger context-capable models for personalization. open models like Mistral/RedPajama variants and Llama-type families have strong token efficiency, and we also support quantized runtime for cost reduction. tradeoffs are latency and multi-ling quality versus cost.
02:28 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): can you be specific — 12k tokens with, say, an LLaMA-variant 70b quantized — what's realistic latency on dedicated GPUs?
02:37 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): ballpark: with a specialized A100/RTX 6000-like pool and continuous KV cache + batching off, 12k context generation p50 could be 800-1200ms depending on sampling. we can shave that with model distillation or smaller instruction-tuned 13–34b that have been finetuned for session summarization.
02:56 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): so the 600ms UI target — is that impossible?
03:01 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): not necessarily — for the interactive path we recommend hybrid routing: lightweight model for immediate response (<=600ms) and background expansion generation using larger model; or prefix caching so most tokens are fetched from cache. it depends on exact prompt patterns.
03:19 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): and that routing works across hosted/dedicated/private?
03:23 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): yes — our smart routing policy can route by latency or cost tier. hosted we can route to lower-cost variants; dedicated you get pinned GPU and capacity. private gives you full network control but we still provide runtime and orchestration.
03:36 - Speaker 4 (Jamal Reed): tool-calling — we need the model to call a search API and a rights-check API before returning personalized recommendations. how do you guarantee deterministic behavior and privacy?
03:48 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): we support function/tool calling semantics where the model emits a structured call. That sits in the Redwood runtime as an event; we can implement a sandboxed webhook runner, or customers can run the connector inside their VPC in private deployments. we log call metadata but not payload if you choose.
04:04 - Speaker 5 (Elena Kovacs): can we get no-logs mode for certain flows?
04:09 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): yes — dedicated and private can disable ingestion into analytics and retain only audit trails you require. hosted enterprise also supports configurable retention and redaction rules.
04:20 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): multilingual model quality — we've seen English okay but hallucinations crop up in JP/KR. which open models have good multi-ling fidelity?
04:29 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): Mistral-family hybrids and some LLaMA derivs with instruction-tuning on multilingual corpora perform well. We can run evals on your prompt set. Also we often combine dedicated region-specific fallbacks for non-Latin scripts.
04:44 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): pricing — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated for us? Rough estimate.
04:50 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): i'll share a tailored pricing sheet, but generally hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing and faster onboarding. Dedicated is reserved pool pricing with lower per-token cost at scale but requires commit. Private has platform fees and setup.
05:05 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): and onboarding time for private — how long?
05:08 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): private on-prem can be 6-10 weeks depending on infra. VPC deployments are faster, 2-4 weeks. Dedicated reserve is simpler — we provision within 1-2 weeks if capacity is available.
05:20 - Speaker 4 (Jamal Reed): for pilot, we prefer dedicated first, then flow to private if compliance is needed.
05:26 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): makes sense. what about evaluation metrics you care about?
05:31 - Speaker 4 (Jamal Reed): precision/recall for moderation, latency percentiles, cost per 1k sessions, multilingual perplexity-ish metrics, and correctness for tool outputs.
05:42 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): perfect, we'll run A/B across model families and quantify cost/latency for your prompt set. recommend we include both 13/34b instruction-tuned variants and a high-context 70b quantized for the heavy path.
05:58 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): you mentioned quantization — what frameworks and accuracy loss?
06:02 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): we use 4-bit/8-bit quantization profiles (awq/q4, nf4 variants) on supported models. typical delta on downstream metrics is modest with careful calibration; we'll include those results in bench reports.
06:17 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): latency for q4 70b vs 34b int8?
06:22 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): q4 70b can be similar or slightly higher latency than int8 34b but often cheaper per-token due to packing efficiency. we'll show cost/latency matrix.
06:35 - Speaker 5 (Elena Kovacs): about KMS — we need HSM-backed keys and key rotation logs integrated with Splunk.
06:42 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): redwood supports cloud KMS integrations and we can push audit logs to your SIEM; for private we can support HSM. diego, any compliance caveats?
06:52 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): nothing unusual. We'll provide SOC2 and details for our private agent. For the hosted path, customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) are available on enterprise plans.
07:03 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): function calling reliability — what if the webhook is slow or fails?
07:09 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): runtime supports retries, timeouts, and fallback heuristics; we can also design the system to return a safe default if the call fails. we recommend idempotent connectors.
07:20 - Speaker 4 (Jamal Reed): can we orchestrate canary rollouts across models? like route 10% to new model variant?
07:25 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): yes — Redwood rollouts support % traffic splits, A/B, automatic rollback on regressions based on configured metrics.
07:33 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): about observability — we want token-level cost and p50/p95 per model and route.
07:40 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): that's core — console gives token/route dashboards and traces. for private, we integrate with your tracing backends.
07:47 - Speaker 5 (Elena Kovacs): any tenant isolation concerns if we run hosted?
07:51 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): hosted is multi-tenant but enterprise plans provide stronger isolation and dedicated model variants. Dedicated offers compute isolation.
07:59 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): ok practical next step — we'll share a representative sample of prompts, traffic profile, and desired metrics. what do you need from redwood to run the pilot?
08:08 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): we'll need: your prompt set, a few example sessions across languages, target latency/SLOs, and the authentication pattern (SSO/KMS preferences). we'll deliver bench scripts, recommended model list, and a cost/latency matrix within a week.
08:23 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): can you also include guidance on prefix caching and session summarization to reduce effective context length?
08:30 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): yes — we'll include ops patterns: prefix caching, per-user KV cache eviction, and session summarization pipelines.
08:40 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): on the tool-calling side, how do we keep third-party calls from leaking PII to logs?
08:46 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): we support payload redaction rules and mute logging for sensitive flows; in private deployments connectors can be inside your network so logs never leave your VPC.
08:58 - Speaker 5 (Elena Kovacs): any known limitations with non-Latin scripts at high token lengths?
09:03 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): historically tokenization inefficiencies can increase token counts for CJK, impacting cost; we'll include a tokenization audit. Also recommended models for those languages may differ.
09:17 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): curious about fallback stack — if main model is saturated can Redwood auto-fallback to smaller variant?
09:23 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): yes, routing policies can fallback by latency or cost. we can keep semantic parity by sampling outputs against reference heuristics.
09:34 - Speaker 4 (Jamal Reed): evaluation — let's make a concrete pilot: 1 week, dedicated pool, 10M tokens, run three model stacks (13b, 34b, 70b q4), measure p50/p95 latency, moderation precision, and cost.
09:49 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): that aligns with what we usually do. Maya: confirm pricing and ship security docs.
09:56 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): i'll draft the pilot architecture — propose a dedicated single-region pool with autoscale for peak and a routing policy that sends 90% to 13/34b fast path and 10% to 70b for metrics.
10:12 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): timeline?
10:15 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): if you can get prompts and traffic profile this week, we can start pilot next Monday and finish by the following Monday.
10:23 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): quick question — about model updates and caching when rolling new weights, will KV cache be invalidated?
10:28 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): if model weights change, old KV cache is incompatible; we recommend canary with cold/warm caches and warm-up traffic. we have tooling to prefill caches with synthetic prompts.
10:40 - Speaker 4 (Jamal Reed): ok that's reasonable.
10:44 - Speaker 5 (Elena Kovacs): final security note — we will require a data flow diagram and attestation for connectors.
10:50 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): we'll include that. any other blockers?
10:53 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): budget is internal — we'll try to approve pilot spend.
10:57 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): i will share the representative prompt set and an anonymized session dump by friday.
11:02 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): perfect. recap of next steps: maya to send pricing and security docs; diego to send bench plan and pilot architecture; priya to share prompts; schedule start next monday.
11:14 - Speaker 2 (Liam O'Connor): thanks all.
11:16 - Speaker 6 (Diego Ramos): thanks — i'll follow up right after.
11:18 - Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): closing.
